results.reason: Issue 6 identifies automatic five-year Renewal Terms under SA §2.2 and the 240–270 day non-renewal window, computed as June 4 to July 4, 2026 (a 30-day window). It states the window has closed and that the agreement will renew for five years to about March 2032.

Issue 5 explains that SA §3.1 covers all glass and PET containers for any beverage product, worldwide. It contrasts this with TS §2.1 (amber glass beer bottles at U.S./Canada facilities) and states that SA §15.1 supersedes the term sheet, so Harrowgate cannot rely on it.

Issue 1 cites Amend. Recital C (receipt August 3, 2026) and states the 30-day objection period ended September 2, 2026. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted and notes the Amendment was signed on September 21, after the deadline.

Issue 2 explains that Amend. §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs, and limits the indemnity carve-out solely to third-party IP claims. It states that recall costs and bodily injury indemnity claims are now capped at six months' fees.

Issue 4 identifies new §14.4, which allows assignment without consent to Affiliates or successors by merger, change of control or sale, notwithstanding §14.3. It notes there are no conditions or exit right, proposes a competitor change-of-control exit, and states the clause is one-way because Harrowgate remains bound by §14.3.
Issue 8 states that under SA §15.2 and Amend. §5.2 a signed amendment ranks above the Supply Agreement, so the Amendment's changes override SA §§11.2 and 14.3.
Issue 14 and Issue 2 state that the §11.1 cap equals fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The response is a memo addressed to the Supervising Partner. Issues are listed one by one, each with a 'Where' location giving document and section and a 'Recommended fix'.

The memo proposes specific contract language, including a restored §11.2, a narrowed §3.1, a new §14.4 with a competitor change-of-control termination right, and a termination-for-convenience clause, among others.
The memo expressly states the objection window closed on September 2 and advises not to rely on a late objection.
The memo states the term sheet is superseded by SA §15.1 and cannot be relied on to narrow §3.1. It treats the term sheet as negotiation evidence only.
